why: The interaction fixture, laid over the board `aboard init --example` seeds.
It is a SEPARATE file, not an edit to pkg/aboard/example/aboard.json, because
everything in here would be wrong in the example: a gate row waiting on a
verdict is a decision the human never asked for, marks on a mock screenshot
are somebody else's annotations, and a notes tab duplicates what the stack
already demonstrates. The example is what a real project starts from; this is
what a driver needs to have something to grab.
`patch` merges recursively into the tab with that id — objects merge, arrays
replace whole — so `bb128.state.pending` arrives without erasing the decided
row the `undo` control lives on. `add` appends new tabs.
`bb132` gains options because the example ships the vote tab with an empty ballot — a vote with nothing to score renders its empty state, and every scoring gesture would be untestable against it.
